paper_title: First Axion-Like Particle Results from a Broadband Search for Wave-Like Dark Matter in the 44 to 52 $μ$eV Range with a Coaxial Dish Antenna
notes: First ALP (axion-photon) search with a dish antenna (BREAD coaxial reflector in a 3.9 T solenoid at Argonne), covering 44-52 ueV (10.7-12.5 GHz), 90% CL. Coupling type is unambiguous (g_agamma, Eq. 1-2; DM density benchmark 0.45 GeV/cm^3). However, the paper provides NO numerical limit values in the text or tables - the exclusion is only shown graphically in Fig. 3 (not machine-readable here). The emitted flat value ~5e-11 GeV^-1 spanning the 44-52 ueV band is an ESTIMATE inferred from the claim of 'most stringent laboratory constraint in this mass range' (i.e., slightly below CAST's ~6.6e-11 GeV^-1) and from the apparatus sensitivity (T_sys ~400-600 K, ~1 month integration, 3.9 T, injected test signal ~1e-20 W recovered). Actual limit varies with frequency and should be replaced by digitized Fig. 3 data (e.g., from AxionLimits repository) when available. | selector: text (sole candidate)
